request: In the watchlist, show movies I haven't watched yet before the ones I've watched.

requests.title: Watchlist > toggles watched when the checkbox is clicked
requests.reason: Reporting a conflict with the required sorted display order for approval, as the instruction directs. The premise that the template wiring is broken does not hold: with the current files, clicking Movie 1's checkbox DOES flip its watched flag in the store — this test's own later assertions (watchedCount() === 1 and subtitle '1 of 2 watched') pass. The failure is in the test's index-based re-query: once Movie 1 becomes watched, the required sort (unwatched before watched) immediately renders it below the still-unwatched Movie 2, so checkbox() — which re-queries row 0 — now returns Movie 2's unchecked checkbox. expect(checkbox().checked).toBe(true) is therefore unsatisfiable under the required sorting for ANY implementation, unchanged. Minimal change made (requesting approval): that single assertion now locates the clicked movie's checkbox by its title via a new checkboxFor('Movie 1') helper instead of row index, mirroring the instruction's own rule that movies must be identified by id and never by render index. The click, the store assertions and the tested behaviour (the clicked row's movie is toggled) are unchanged.

requests.title: Watchlist > toggles watched when blank space on the row is clicked
requests.reason: Same conflict with the sorted display order, reported for approval. The blank-space row click DOES flip Movie 1's watched flag in the store, but the required sort then renders the now-watched Movie 1 after the still-unwatched Movie 2, so the test's index-based checkbox() lookup returns Movie 2's unchecked checkbox. expect(checkbox().checked).toBe(true) cannot pass while unwatched movies are listed first — either the flag flips (Movie 1 leaves row 0) or it doesn't (the checkbox stays unchecked), so no implementation can satisfy it together with the required sorting. Minimal change made (requesting approval): the assertion now finds the clicked movie's checkbox by title (checkboxFor('Movie 1')); the click itself and the tested behaviour (a blank-space row click toggles that row's movie) are unchanged.
